sources.name: OpenAI News
sources.note: Company announcements; about 2 a day. Press articles link here as the primary source.

sources.name: OpenAI Deployment Safety Hub
sources.note: System cards, one per OpenAI model launch, newest first. openai.com/index/* refuses the scanner (403), this host does not. One entry per scan so the first scan takes only the newest card, never the back catalogue.

sources.name: Google AI blog
sources.note: Google product and research AI announcements on blog.google.

sources.name: Google DeepMind blog
sources.note: Model and research releases; a few a week.

sources.name: Anthropic news
sources.note: No RSS feed; the news index page is read as an HTML listing. Model launches live at the site root (/claude-opus-5-5, /claude-sonnet-5-5), not under /news/, hence the second prefix (2026-09-30).

sources.name: Claude blog
sources.note: Anthropic's product blog (Claude apps, Claude Code, connectors); no RSS. Separate from anthropic.com/news, which carries company and model announcements.

sources.name: Hugging Face blog
sources.note: Open-model releases; many posts are tutorials the writer will decline.

sources.name: NVIDIA blog
sources.note: AI and hardware announcements; the vertical is chosen per story.

sources.name: Apple Newsroom
sources.note: Apple product and platform announcements.

sources.name: Microsoft official blog
sources.note: Company announcements. The separate AI feed (blogs.microsoft.com/ai/feed/) answered 4xx on 2026-09-24.

sources.name: Ethereum Foundation blog
sources.note: Protocol upgrades and network announcements; low volume.

sources.name: CFTC press releases
sources.note: US derivatives regulator; most releases are not about crypto and are declined by the writer. SEC press releases were left out: their pages extract to a 248-character access notice.

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.note: Press; roughly 15 stories a day. The story is div.entry-content: <main> also holds the Related and Latest in AI cards with relative times and a rotating event promo, which re-render every half hour.

sources.name: Ars Technica AI
sources.note: Press; a few stories a day. The main feeds.arstechnica.com feed is refused by robots.txt.

sources.name: The Verge AI
sources.note: Press; the feed only carries the latest ten stories. The traffic-ranked Most Popular rail sits inside <article> (duet--layout--rail) and reorders several times an hour; More in AI and Top Stories are duet--layout--article-recirc.

sources.name: CoinDesk
sources.note: Press; much of it is market commentary, which the writer declines. The story is div.document-body: <main> also holds Latest Crypto News with relative ages and, now and then, Russian UI labels. premium-hide drops the live price chips inside paragraphs (BTC$83,034.73, sometimes in Russian number format), captions and the video slot.

sources.name: The Block
sources.note: Press; policy and industry coverage.

sources.name: Meta Newsroom
sources.note: Meta's own announcements, Llama and AI products included; added 2026-09-26 at the owner's request.

sources.name: AWS Machine Learning Blog
sources.note: Amazon's cloud AI launches; many posts are how-tos, which the writer declares not newsworthy.

sources.name: Microsoft Research blog
sources.note: Microsoft Research papers and model releases.

sources.name: Google Keyword blog
sources.note: All of Google's official blog (Android, Pixel, Search), wider than the AI section above; the same post from both feeds is an exact duplicate.

sources.name: Google Cloud blog
sources.note: Google Cloud announcements; the feed's articles live on cloud.google.com.

sources.name: GitHub blog
sources.note: GitHub's announcements, Copilot and developer AI tools included.

sources.name: Cloudflare blog
sources.note: Cloudflare's announcements and incident write-ups.

sources.name: SEC press releases
sources.note: US regulator; most releases are not about crypto and the writer declares those not newsworthy.

sources.name: Chainalysis blog
sources.note: On-chain research and hack reports; first-party for its own findings. The story sits outside <article> and <main>; those hold only the related-posts cards.

sources.name: Decrypt
sources.note: Press; a second website for crypto stories, which automatic publication can count.

sources.name: Taiwan MODA press releases
sources.note: 數位發展部新聞稿. The press-release list URL is a 404; the home page lists the five newest, newest first. Needs fetch.tls_context (TWCA chain fails Python 3.13's strict X.509 mode).

sources.name: Taiwan FSC press releases (crypto)
sources.note: 金管會新聞稿, only the crypto ones: most FSC releases are funds, insurance and statistics. The RSS page lists no feed URL; the news list page is read instead, news items told apart from the menu by their query string. maincontent keeps the release and drops the page's view counter, which would change the evidence hash on every fetch. Needs fetch.tls_context.
